newsitem.title: UK: Brit Biotech says lead drugs on target.
newsitem.headline: Brit Biotech says lead drugs on target.

text.p: British Biotech Plc said on Wednesday that its losses grew in the year to April 30 as spending rose on developing its lead drugs for cancer and pancreatitis.

The company, which is seen as the UK's flagship biotechnology group, announced a pre-tax loss of 28.9 million pounds ($48.8 million), up from 25.2 million pounds a year earlier, but said both of its key projects were on target.

The Oxford-based company's biggest hope is anti-cancer drug Marimastat, the first of a new generation of cancer drugs known as MMP inhibitors. British Biotech said it was starting late-stage trials of Marimastat in two additional cancers, non-small cell lung cancer and ovarian cancer.
The drug is already being tested in small cell lung cancer, brain cancer, stomach cancer and pancreatic cancer, although results from the trials are unlikely to be ready before 1999.

Losses widened, partly because of costs linked to setting up an international sales force for its lead product Zacutex, a drug to treat inflammation of the pancreas, which it hopes to put on the market in Europe in 1998.

British Biotech also named a new finance director to replace James Noble, who left unexpectedly earlier this year. It said Malcolm Fallen would join the company in September from British Telecommunications Plc. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
